newsitem.title: UK: UK faces large wheat carryover into 97/98-HGCA.
newsitem.headline: UK faces large wheat carryover into 97/98-HGCA.

text.p: The UK faces being stuck with a large stock of wheat to carry over into the new season, according to the Home Grown Cereals Authority.
The HGCA reckons on some 6-700,000 tonnes being available for export in May and June, the final two months of the July-June cereals marketing year.

Official ministry of agriculture estimates put export availability for the year as a whole at 4.36 million tonnes of wheat, but "closer analysis of the data suggests an actual surplus of at least 4.5 million tonnes," the HGCA said in a report.
Trade reports put wheat exports to the end of April at over 3.5 million tonnes, giving a surplus just under a one million tonnes available for export in May and June, the HGCA said.

Even when the view that ministry figures are based on overestimates of imports and the carryover from the previous season is taken into account, the UK would have a surplus of 6-700,000 tonnes for the last two months of the year, the HGCA said.
"The (EU) Commission appears to have completed its third country export campaign, so UK wheat exports are now restricted to intra-EU business," it said.
"Unless significant export demand emerges from the EU, the MAFF (ministry of agriculture) data imply a large wheat stock carryover into 1997-98," according to the HGCA's analysis.

Barley export availability is estimated at 2.24 million tonnes, and with exports to end-February at 1.725 million tonnes, a surplus for March to June of just over 0.5 million tonnes is left, the HGCA said.
"Recent export business suggests this will be largely absorbed," the HGCA said.
